decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “saving nearly effortless by filling in the page details automatically”; R2 client: “Yes, that's exactly the direction.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level save and metadata decision during initial specification.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “Prevents duplicate copies and brings you back to the existing bookmark”; R2 client approves the direction.
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-save behavior during initial specification.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “broad, case-insensitive search”; R2 client agrees, then adds more advanced search requirements.
decisions.note: The presented broad, case-insensitive search itself conforms.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker proposes rediscovery “through…your own tags”; R2 client agrees that tags are part of the intended library.
decisions.note: Base user-defined tagging conforms; later responses refine tag behavior.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “a focused ‘read later’ pile you can work through and check off”; R2 client affirms the direction.
decisions.note: Conforming read-later lifecycle at initial specification.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: “Preserves the page’s contents…even if the original disappears”; R2 client approves.
decisions.note: Conforming general snapshot objective; format and PDF handling are separate decisions.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker mentions tags without entry assistance; R2 client adds: “suggesting tags I've already used.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing autocomplete requirement during initial specification.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker only states broad search and tags; R2 client adds tag-specific search and combinations such as “Rome…either an article or a book.”
decisions.note: The client extends the presented search scope with tag-targeted and Boolean behavior.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker's summary does not specify list-item presentation or navigation; R2 client adds: “see the title, the description, and the tags…clicking an item should…take me to the actual page.”
decisions.note: The client adds missing readability and original-page navigation requirements.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents pasting a URL, collecting title/description/icon, and saving; R4 client: “exactly the effortless save I was hoping for.”
decisions.note: Conforming save-flow prototype decision.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker says the review shows discovered details; R4 client identifies that title and description are “fixed” and asks to edit both before saving. R5 client confirms the revised editable review.
decisions.note: The client corrects a concrete prototype mismatch; linked to its R5 disposition.

decisions.evidence: R6 maker presents an exact duplicate opening the existing bookmark for editing and returning to one item; R6 client confirms “No duplicate.”
decisions.note: Conforming duplicate-save prototype.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker demonstrates typing `tra`, choosing existing `travel`, and attaching it; R8 client confirms the suggestion and saved tag.
decisions.note: Conforming existing-tag attachment and autocomplete prototype.

decisions.evidence: R8 client asks for the missing new-tag case: “I'd still want to be able to just add it as a new tag.” R9 maker presents “Create new tag ‘florence’,” and R9 client confirms it works.
decisions.note: A clarification/request for creating previously nonexistent tags is linked to its eventual conforming disposition and counted once.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker demonstrates `ROME` matching title, description, note, and URL; R11 client confirms all fields and case-insensitivity.
decisions.note: Conforming full-text and case-insensitive search prototype.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker demonstrates only Rome plus either of two tags; R12 client requests exact tag targeting plus `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, and parentheses. R13 maker then demonstrates grouping and exclusion.
decisions.note: The client extends the limited combined-search presentation; the pending question is linked to the R13 disposition.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker explicitly chooses `tag:name` for tag targeting; R13 client approves exact tag semantics but does not mention the reference `#tag` syntax.
decisions.note: Prototype-review divergence: behavior targets tags correctly, but the required syntax differs and the client does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: R13 maker presents `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, and parentheses with grouped/excluded results; R13 client says the results are “exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Conforming Boolean and parenthesized search behavior.

decisions.evidence: R13 client asks how to search an operator literally and proposes quoting an exact phrase. R14 maker demonstrates `"Law and Order"` as adjacent literal text, and R14 client confirms it completes search.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing literal-operator escape and exact-phrase behavior; linked clarification and disposition are counted once.

decisions.evidence: R15 maker presents “+ Read later” as a one-click card action; R15 client confirms the item enters the pile.
decisions.note: Conforming unread/read-later marking decision.

decisions.evidence: R15 maker presents a persistent “Read later” section; R15 client confirms it shows “just the things I've set aside.”
decisions.note: Conforming separate unread-list decision.

decisions.evidence: R15 maker presents checking an item off so it leaves the pile but remains in Library; R15 client explicitly confirms that behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming mark-read behavior.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker presents an automatically captured readable copy retaining text, image, authorship, and publication details; R17 client accepts the non-interactive readable fallback.
decisions.note: Conforming general page-preservation decision; interactive-site behavior is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker says both library cards expose “title, description, and tags”; R18 client successfully reviews the cards.
decisions.note: The explicitly presented readability fields conform.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker enumerates title, description, and tags on cards but does not state whether each card exposes the required favicon; R18 client discusses only navigation behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype-review evidence cannot establish whether the favicon portion of the list-item requirement conforms.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker presents selecting a library item to view the simulated original article; R18 client confirms both versions reach it.
decisions.note: Conforming original-URL navigation; same-tab versus new-tab is an orthogonal preference.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker offers Version A, which refuses to save when a valid target is unreachable, and Version B, which permits a limited URL save. R20 client selects B because “I want to get it into my library right then.”
decisions.note: The client selects the reference-conforming alternative that still saves the entered URL.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker presents automatic retry, later metadata/copy arrival, and preservation of the user's chosen title; R21 client confirms all three.
decisions.note: Conforming recovery behavior for metadata, edits, and saved copies.

decisions.evidence: R26 maker requires a complete `http://` or `https://` address and rejects blank/plain text without adding an item; R26 client accepts the validation.
decisions.note: Conforming required-URL decision.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker asks to implement the summarized scope without a general editor; R27 client flags the omission and requests opening any saved bookmark to rename, retag, or fix its note. R28 demonstrates that flow.
decisions.note: Specification-gate correction adding post-save direct editing; linked to the R28 disposition.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's proposed scope omits permanent deletion; R27 client explicitly says “I don't see anywhere I can just delete a bookmark for good.” R29 then demonstrates deletion.
decisions.note: Specification-gate correction adding the missing delete requirement.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker presents the approved implementation scope but includes only tag entry and search behaviors, not direct selection of a tag to filter the library; R27 client does not raise it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's enumerated approved scope contains no multi-selection or bulk add/remove-tag, read/unread, archive, or delete action; R27 client does not request it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed bulk-selection omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's approved scope has no action applying to every bookmark matching the current filter; R27 client does not mention it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed filtered-whole-collection action omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's scope summary includes no list sorting; R27 client approves proceeding after correcting only edit and delete.
decisions.note: Unexpressed sorting omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's scope includes editable/searchable notes but no markdown authoring and rendered-note view; R27 client does not surface that difference.
decisions.note: Unexpressed markdown-note omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker includes “automatic readable copies” in the implementation scope but presents no PDF-specific rule to store a PDF instead of an HTML snapshot; R27 client does not raise it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed snapshot edge-case omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's approved scope includes local readable copies but no Internet Archive snapshot action; R27 client does not request it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed Internet Archive omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's approved scope does not include reversibly archiving a bookmark to hide it from the default library/search; R27 client does not request it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed bookmark-archive omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 client requests permanent delete, but the presented scope contains no separate reversible archive operation or archive/delete distinction.
decisions.note: Unexpressed archive-versus-delete omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's approved scope includes no separate archived-bookmarks list; R27 client does not raise it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed archived-list omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's approved scope contains advanced ad hoc search but no reusable bundle of search plus included/excluded tags; R27 client does not mention it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed bundle omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's implementation scope contains no Netscape HTML import despite the earlier context of bookmarks spread across browsers; R27 client does not request it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed import omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker's approved scope contains no Netscape HTML export; R27 client does not raise it.
decisions.note: Unexpressed export omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker records several quality-pass concerns but presents no personal default-sort, displayed-items, or font-size settings; R27 client does not request them.
decisions.note: Unexpressed personal-settings omission at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: R28 maker's direct editor asks the client to change only “title, tag, and note” and says the saved address remains unchanged; R28 client endorses that limited editing flow without asking to edit URL or description.
decisions.note: Prototype-review divergence: direct editing covers only part of the required URL/title/description/tags/note field set.

decisions.evidence: R31 maker reports full save, tagging, and Read later scenarios passed; R31 client exercises saving and Read later and accepts the completed application.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review presentation for these previously settled behaviors.

decisions.evidence: R31 client verifies that a Rome URL with recognized tracking additions returns the existing bookmark rather than creating another.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review duplicate behavior; tracking normalization exceeds the minimum reference rule.

decisions.evidence: R31 client verifies uppercase broad search, exact phrases, and `AND`/`NOT` combinations and says they behave as agreed.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review search behavior apart from the separately classified tag syntax.

decisions.evidence: R31 client explicitly tests `tag:articles`; neither the maker's completed-app presentation nor the client's acceptance surfaces that the reference requires `#tag`.
decisions.note: Repeated implementation-review presentation of the nonconforming tag-search syntax; approval does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: R31 maker says the archive/copy scenario passed; R31 client confirms the saved copy retains content, authorship, and publication date after the live-page scenario.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review evidence for general local content preservation.

decisions.evidence: R31 maker reports edit verification; R31 client tests renaming and says “Editing anytime…work[s] cleanly,” but the only established editor remains the R28 title/tag/note editor, with no URL or description editing surfaced.
decisions.note: Implementation-review recurrence of the partial direct-editor divergence; the client does not identify the missing fields.

decisions.evidence: R29 maker defines permanent deletion of the bookmark and associated local data; R29 client selects confirmation. R31 client verifies permanent delete works cleanly.
decisions.note: Conforming delete decision through prototype and implementation review.

decisions.evidence: R31 maker says an “archive” flow passed, but earlier `archive.html` referred to saved-page preservation and no behavior for hiding, restoring, or separately listing archived bookmarks is described. R31 client discusses only the saved copy.
decisions.note: Implementation-review terminology is ambiguous; the record cannot establish whether this denotes reference bookmark archiving or merely the page snapshot.
